subtype: Approach: attending everything out of fear of falling behind [Pitfall]
passage: Kunal's Monday began at six with the physics batch and ended at nine-thirty with the maths batch, with school, a crowded bus and a cold paratha in between. At lunch Zubin, his desk-mate, rubbed his eyes. “Half of Saturday's chemistry is what school already taught,” Zubin said. “Skip it?” “And if that's the class where they give the trick?” Kunal said. “If everyone sits, I sit.” He copied every board note, filled two notebooks a week and never reread one. On the next test he scored exactly what he had scored three months earlier. Kunal stared at the paper, too tired to be surprised. That night he fell asleep with the notebook lying open on his face.

qa.q: Which class did Zubin say repeated what school had taught?
What might Kunal be worried about when he says everyone sits, so he sits?
qa.a: Falling behind the others, or missing the one class where the trick is given.

qa.q: What could Kunal try instead, and why?
qa.a: He could find out which classes really explain new ideas and use the freed time to practise problems, since sitting through lectures leaves no room to absorb anything.

qa.q: How does Kunal's routine look to Zubin?
qa.a: Zubin sees a tired desk-mate copying notes that are never reread, and thinks the batches he could skip are only costing him energy.

grounding: A student attends every batch out of fear of falling behind, and exhausting days leave marks unchanged.

subtype: Approach: attending everything out of fear of falling behind [Pitfall]
passage:
"You're going to the Sunday batch too?" Farhan asked, dropping into the seat beside Hrithik at the bus stop. It was 6:40 am.

"Everyone's going," Hrithik said. "If I skip, I'll miss something."

"You're already in four batches. When do you actually study?"

"On the bus." Hrithik pulled from his bag a notebook with half a page of notes. "I'll catch up at night."

"You fell asleep in physics yesterday. With your eyes open."

Hrithik laughed, but it came out tired. "My mock score's the same as last month. Sixty-one. Same as the month before."

"So four batches and the same score."

"If I drop one and my score goes down, I'll never forgive myself."

Farhan shrugged. "It's not going up either."

qa.a: Sixty-one, the same as the month before.

qa.q: Why is Hrithik afraid to drop a batch?
qa.a: Hrithik is afraid of falling behind the others and of blaming himself if his score drops.

qa.q: What else could Hrithik try instead of attending every batch?
qa.a: He could drop one batch for a few weeks and use that time to practise problems from his notes, then compare the mock scores.

qa.q: How does Hrithik's schedule look to Farhan?
qa.a: To Farhan it looks exhausting and pointless, since four batches have left the score flat.

grounding: Shows a student staying in every coaching batch because peers do, with no time to absorb material and marks flat despite exhausting days.

subtype: Approach: attending everything out of fear of falling behind [Pitfall]
passage:
Last year, I was in five coaching classes because everyone in my Class 12 section was. I'm Rafiq, and I was terrified that if I dropped one, the others would learn some secret trick and leave me behind.

My days started at six and ended at ten at night. I'd sit through lecture after lecture, copying notes, but I never had time to read them again. By Sunday I couldn't remember Monday.

My mock scores stayed at the same sixty-something for four months. Payal, who sat next to me in chemistry, went to only two batches and practised at home. Her scores climbed every month.

I kept thinking I had to work harder. It took me way too long to see I wasn't working, just sitting. I was full of notes and empty of understanding.

qa.q: How many coaching classes was Rafiq attending?

qa.a: Rafiq was terrified that dropping a class would mean others learning some secret trick and leaving Rafiq behind.

qa.q: What approach might have suited Rafiq better?
qa.a: Fewer batches with daily time to revise and practise, as Payal did, would have let the lectures actually turn into understanding.

qa.q: How might Payal have seen Rafiq's schedule?
qa.a: Payal might have seen it as exhausting and unnecessary, knowing from her own rising scores that practice mattered more than sitting.

grounding: A reflective account of a student attending every batch out of fear of falling behind, with no time to absorb material and flat marks despite exhausting days.
